question:
Initially, a certain amount of $\text{P(g)}$ was placed in an empty container. The hypothetical reaction reaches equilibrium in a closed container according to the following balanced equation:
$$\text{P(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{Q(g)} \quad \Delta H < 0$$
At time $t$, the temperature is increased.

Which graph below best illustrates the resulting changes in the rates of the forward and reverse reactions after the temperature is increased?

A Graph A
B Graph B
C Graph C
D Graph D
memo:
B $\checkmark\checkmark$

*Rationale: An increase in temperature increases the average kinetic energy of all reacting particles, causing the rates of BOTH the forward and reverse reactions to increase instantaneously at time $t$. According to Le Chatelier's principle, an increase in temperature favours the endothermic reaction. Since the forward reaction is exothermic ($\Delta H < 0$), the reverse reaction is endothermic. Therefore, the reverse reaction rate (solid line) increases by a greater magnitude than the forward reaction rate (dashed line), and a new equilibrium is re-established at higher rates (Option B).*
